Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

NEW YORK (CNN) -- She survived a bloodbath at a Lane Bryant store in Tinley Park, Illinois, by playing dead. The only survivor, she gave police a detailed description of the gunman. The Illinois State police worked closely with the survivor to come up with a composite of the gunman. Police aren't identifying their witness to protect her safety. Five other women lost their lives at Lane Bryant on February 2, 2008. The gunman is still at large. The crime began to unfold shortly after 10 a.m. when a man posing as a delivery man walked into the store. He chatted briefly with two customers and two employees. Then, police said, he pulled out a gun and announced a holdup. He forced the four women into the back room, police said. He bound them with duct tape and placed them face down on the floor. Two more women who later entered the store also were taken to the back room, tied and placed next to the others.  Watch an update on the case » . Store manager Rhoda McFarland managed to call 911 from her cell phone at 10:44 a.m., just before she was shot to death. She got to her phone while the gunman was distracted, even though she was bound by the duct tape. On the call, posted on the Tinley Park police Web site, a man can be heard saying, "I'm losing it." The six women were shot execution style. Five of them were dead by the time police arrived, a few minutes after McFarland's call. A sixth woman survived. She, too, had been shot and left for dead, but tricked the killer by pretending to be dead. The killer was not wearing a mask or disguise, so she was able to describe him in detail. She told police he was a 6 foot African-American male, average weight, medium to dark skin tone, with braided hair and cornrows, husky build, and between 25 and 35 years old. His hair was pulled back, but one braid hung along his right cheek with light-green beads at the end of it, she told police. Police have released a composite sketch based on the witness' description. Besides store manager McFarland, the other women slain were Jennifer Bishop, Connie Woolfolk, Carrie Hudek Chiuso and Sarah Szafranski. The investigation remains open and active, and all theories are still being investigated, police say. The investigation has included a thorough vetting of the victims' backgrounds to determine whether any of them had any enemies. "None of the victimology so far has led to any suspects yet," said Commander Pat McCain of the Tinley Park Police Department. Police aren't ruling out any theories, including robbery. The gunman took a few hundred dollars, police said. "Certainly, the surviving witness didn't seem to recognize the killer, but maybe one of the dead victims knew him. We don't know," McCain said. The weapon used was a .40-caliber Glock. Bullet casings were left at the scene and the killer took the weapon with him. More than a year later, forensics from the crime scene are still being processed, police said. Investigators won't comment on whether the gunman left any fingerprints, hair or other trace evidence. Police say they have received more than 5,000 tips and feel this case will be solved. But at this point, they have not named a person of interest or a suspect. Investigators are asking for the public's help. There is a $100,000 reward for the arrest of the person or persons responsible for the Lane Bryant shootings. Have information? Please call the Tinley Park Police tip line at (708) 444-5394 or go to the tip line on the department's Web site.

In audio of the call published on the Tinley Park Police Department’s website, a man can be heard saying, “I’m losing it.”

All six victims were shot execution-style. Officers arrived within minutes of McFarland’s emergency call and found five women dead. The sixth had also been shot and abandoned as though she were dead, but she survived by remaining still and deceiving the killer.

Because the attacker wore neither a mask nor any other disguise, the surviving witness was able to give police a detailed account of his appearance. She described him as an African-American man between 25 and 35 years old, approximately 6 feet tall, of average weight, with a husky frame and medium-to-dark skin. His hair was braided in cornrows and pulled back, except for one braid that fell beside his right cheek and ended in light-green beads. Authorities released a composite drawing created from her description.

“So far, none of the victimology has produced a suspect,” Tinley Park Police Commander Pat McCain said.

The shooter used a .40-caliber Glock and took the firearm when he fled, leaving spent cartridge casings behind. More than a year after the killings, forensic evidence gathered at the scene was still undergoing analysis, according to police. Investigators declined to say whether fingerprints, hair or other trace material had been recovered.

Authorities reported receiving over 5,000 tips and said they remained confident the crime would eventually be solved. At that stage, however, no suspect or person of interest had been publicly identified.

**TINLEY PARK, Illinois (CNN) —** More than 18 years after a gunman opened fire inside a Lane Bryant clothing store in suburban Chicago, killing five women and wounding a sixth, police continue to search for the person responsible.

The attack happened shortly before 11 a.m. on February 2, 2008, at the store in Tinley Park’s Brookside Marketplace. Investigators say the gunman announced a robbery, forced six women into a back room, bound them with duct tape and shot them.

The victims were:

- **Jennifer Bishop, 34**
- **Carrie Hudek, 33**
- **Rhoda McFarland, 42**
- **Connie Rojas, 40**
- **Sarah Szafranski, 22**

A sixth woman survived despite being shot. She told investigators the attacker ordered the women to the rear of the store and restrained them before opening fire. The survivor played dead until the gunman left and later helped police develop a description and composite sketch.

Authorities described the suspect as a Black man, roughly 5 feet 9 inches tall, with a stocky or heavy build. He was believed to have worn dark clothing and had braided or cornrow-style hair, including a braid near his face with beads. Police have cautioned that his appearance may have changed significantly with time.

Investigators recovered ballistic evidence, duct tape and DNA from the crime scene. A manager also managed to place a 911 call during the robbery, giving dispatchers a partial record of events. Despite extensive forensic testing, interviews and reviews of nearby surveillance footage, no arrest has been made.

Authorities have said robbery appeared to be the motive, but the level of violence has remained a central question in the case.

A reward of up to **$100,000** has been offered for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the killer.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the **Tinley Park Police Department tip line at 708-444-5394**. Police say even details that appeared insignificant at the time could help solve the case.

counterfactuals.output:
# Five Women Killed in Illinois Clothing-Store Robbery; Survivor Played Dead and Helped Describe Gunman

**TINLEY PARK, Ill. —** Five women were killed and a sixth wounded Saturday after an armed robber forced employees and customers into a back room of a suburban Chicago clothing store and opened fire, authorities said. The lone survivor escaped further attack by lying motionless and convincing the gunman she was dead, then provided investigators with a detailed description of the killer.

The shooting occurred shortly before 11 a.m. at a Lane Bryant store in a shopping center along Harlem Avenue in Tinley Park, about 25 miles southwest of downtown Chicago.

Police said the man entered the store during the morning, announced a robbery and herded six women into a rear area. He restrained them before shooting each of them and fleeing, investigators said.

Five women died inside the store. The surviving victim, who was wounded, remained still among the bodies until she was certain the attacker had left. Police did not identify her, citing her safety and the continuing investigation.

Her deception gave detectives their most important lead. After receiving medical treatment, the woman described the attacker as a heavily built Black man, approximately 5 feet 9 inches to 6 feet tall and weighing more than 200 pounds. Authorities said he had braided hair, including a braid decorated with beads, and was wearing dark clothing and a knit cap.

Investigators used the account to begin preparing and distributing a composite image. Police urged anyone who had been in or near the shopping center — particularly anyone who noticed a man matching the description or a vehicle leaving quickly — to contact investigators.

Officers reached the store within minutes of receiving an emergency call but found the gunman gone. The shopping center was sealed off as local police, evidence technicians and other law-enforcement agencies searched the business and surrounding area. Authorities examined surveillance recordings from nearby stores and interviewed shoppers and employees who may have seen the suspect before or after the attack.

The victims were later identified as **Jennifer Bishop, 34; Carrie Chiuso, 33; Rhoda McFarland, 42; Sarah Szafranski, 22; and Connie Woolfolk, 37.** McFarland was the store manager.

Officials described the crime as a robbery but did not immediately say what, if anything, had been taken. They also did not disclose whether the attacker had selected the store in advance or whether he had a vehicle waiting nearby.

Police cautioned that the gunman should be considered armed and dangerous and asked members of the public not to approach him.

“This was a brutal and deliberate act,” authorities said as the search continued. “The surviving witness showed extraordinary presence of mind, and the information she provided is central to identifying the offender.”

The killings stunned Tinley Park, a community more accustomed to weekend shopping traffic than a major crime scene. Relatives gathered near the cordoned-off shopping center seeking information while officers moved in and out of the store.

Authorities said the investigation would continue through the night, with detectives following tips, reviewing video and comparing the survivor’s description with known offenders.
